content: Mittelschmerz refers to a one-sided, lower abdominal pain experienced by women around the time of ovulation, which is when an egg is released from the ovaries. The pain associated with Mittelschmerz can alternate sides from one month to the next or remain on the same side for several months. It is typically described as a sharp, cramping, and distinctive pain that lasts anywhere from a few minutes to several hours, though in some cases it may persist for up to 24-48 hours. Severe pain is rare. This discomfort usually occurs midway through the menstrual cycle. The cause of Mittelschmerz is linked to ovulation. Approximately 20% of women experience this type of ovulation-related pain. The pain may occur just before, during, or after ovulation. Before ovulation, the growth of the ovarian follicle may stretch the surface of the ovary, leading to discomfort. During ovulation, the rupture of the follicle releases fluid or blood, which can irritate the abdominal lining and result in pain. It is important to seek medical attention if the nature of the ovulation pain changes, if it lasts longer than usual, or if it is accompanied by vaginal bleeding. A healthcare provider may perform a pelvic examination to rule out other issues. If the pain persists, additional diagnostic tests, such as an abdominal ultrasound or a transvaginal pelvic ultrasound, may be conducted to investigate other potential causes of ovarian or pelvic pain. In most cases, no specific treatment is required for Mittelschmerz. However, pain relievers (analgesics) may be used to manage prolonged or intense pain. Mittelschmerz is not harmful and does not indicate the presence of any disease. In fact, women who experience this pain may find it helpful for family planning, as it signals the time of ovulation. A woman is most likely to conceive just before, during, or immediately after ovulation. There are typically no complications associated with Mittelschmerz. For women who wish to prevent ovulation-related pain, birth control pills can be used to suppress ovulation and alleviate the associated discomfort.
